evidence: Structural monotonicity holds. (1) Scoring function: task/tests/tools/score.py and task/tests/scoring.toml are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff -r of tests/tools and diff of scoring.toml/test.sh produced no output). score.py computes gates_passed = all(score > 0.0) for render/constraints, floors_passed = functional > 0.05, weighted = 0.6*F + 0.2*P + 0.2*V, reward = weighted only if gates and floor pass, else 0. Every term is non-decreasing in every dimension score, so if app A scores >= app B on every gate and dimension, reward(A) >= reward(B): no Pareto inversion is possible from weights, gates or floor. Gates carry 0.0 mass (scoring.toml [gates]), so passing only the cheap gates earns nothing. (2) Mass: functional 0.6 outweighs polish+visual 0.4 combined; per-dimension criterion weights: functional 43 binary criteria summing 58.5 (min 0.5, max 2.5), polish 5 binary summing 12.0, visual 5 likert summing 6.0 (each 1.2). (3) Polish is not cheap craft that a non-working app can farm: hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (3+3 of 12) are scored 0 if the live update does not arrive ('If no update arrives within 15 seconds, preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0'), hro_pol_failed_send and hro_pol_session_resume carry positive controls ('it is sent once'; 'the same conversation's reply is as left and sends, which is the positive control'), so polish co-varies with real function rather than inverting it. (4) Refusal-farming check (do-nothing app passing negative rows): every functional refusal row names a positive control - e.g. hro_activity_refusals 'The successful actions' lines are the control', hro_undo_once 'a successful undo is the control', hro_anonymous 'A signed-in success of each is the control', hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_stale_refused, hro_interview_full, hro_undo_full, hro_add_email_rules, hro_job_open - and hro_candidate_private states 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'; functional/prompt.md:30 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'. A broken app that refuses everything therefore cannot outscore a working one on these rows. (5) Stricter-better-app failing a gate: the constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23) only demands behaviour the brief requires (recruiter opens job with places, adds candidate, Observer reads board - hireops_rules.md:18 'Observer | reads the board...'), allows another working staff account, and grading prompts say UI refusal hiding is the app's choice; render gate only needs wrong-password refusal then valid sign-in. No gate penalises a more correct app. (6) Double-counting that could invert order within a dimension is guarded: functional/prompt.md:40 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', visual/prompt.md:104 likewise; focus-on-refusal (hro_refused_put_back) is backed by hireops_rules.md:85 so a conforming app is not penalised for following the rules. Residual (Note, not a defect): because the profile-fixed linear 0.6/0.2/0.2 blend and template floor 0.05 trade dimensions, a non-dominated pair can rank against intuition, e.g. F=0.10,P=0,V=1.0 -> 0.26 vs F=0.40,P=0,V=0 -> 0.24; a nearly non-functional app that clears the 0.05 floor (2.925 of 58.5 functional weight, roughly two criteria) can collect the full 0.2 visual mass because the visual gate in visual/prompt.md:102 zeroes only a blank/static shell or a failed creation+Observer check. Weights and floor are template/profile-controlled (scoring.toml identical to template), so this is not a task-fixable defect. Risk=true because: the raw-evidence-index scope explicitly says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent', so no measured ranking of graded variants (golden vs. degraded apps) exists, judge-noise-induced inversions are unmeasured, and the workbook internal note marks this row for monitoring.
counterexample: Attempted: (a) broken app that could pass - a refuse-everything server: blocked by named positive controls on every refusal row and by the constraints gate requiring a real shared write; a pretty near-empty shell: blocked by gate+floor unless it genuinely clears ~5% of functional weight, in which case it can still gain up to 0.2 visual (profile-level trade-off, recorded as Note). (b) conforming alternative that could fail - an app that hides disallowed controls, refuses in UI before sending, or keeps drafts server-side: criteria explicitly accept these ('hiding it is optional', 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes', 'Where drafts are kept is yours'). No task-specific inversion found.
suggested_fix: None required for task files. To retire the residual risk, owner should obtain measured ranking evidence (configured judge runs on golden plus at least one deliberately degraded variant, e.g. live updates removed, showing golden > degraded) before claiming discrimination; any floor change is template/profile-controlled and needs lead authorization.
